answer: An agent economy can give every identity a lease that expires unless renewed by fresh graded work: a willow branch bends but does not hold forever, and each identity must send a new signal of real work each epoch — a pulse of attested contributions — or its lease lapses and its locked stake burns. A farm cannot park a thousand fakes and harvest them later; every extra head needs its own steady pulse of new work, so the cost of the thousandth fake is a thousandth stream of real labor, renewed forever.
